Petroleum and intermediate-goods imports recorded strong growth, while capital-machinery imports declined more than 7 per cent, according to Bangladesh Bank data.

title: Brazil reviews PSF duties up to $391 per tonne: Will Asia gain more?
summary:
Brazil’s SECEX has opened a review that could suspend or modify duties on polyester staple fibre imports from China, India, Thailand and Vietnam.
ABINT sought the public-interest review after Indorama closed its Cabo de Santo Agostinho plant, reducing domestic supply.
Evidence is due by December 21, 2026; antidumping duties of $74.98-$390.94 per tonne apply with a 16 per cent import tariff.

title: Paraxylene falls 11% in two weeks as crude cools, mills hold back
summary:
Asian paraxylene fell close to 11 per cent from November 3 to 17, with CFR Southeast Asia closing at $1.21/kg as PTA moved lower in step.
FOB Korea dropped 11.16 per cent and CFR Taiwan lost 10.98 per cent after a sharp mid-period swing, while buyers favoured small prompt lots.
Cheaper crude, naphtha and calmer Middle East headlines weakened costs; polyester mills avoided forward cover.

title: North India cotton yarn remains under pressure, prices down in Delhi
summary:
North India’s cotton yarn market stayed under pressure as weak downstream demand, tight payments and poor export orders dragged Delhi prices down by ₹3 (~$0.03) per kg.
Ludhiana held steady after last week’s correction, while Panipat recycled yarn remained bearish despite waste shortages and lower imports from Bangladesh.
Cotton fell by ₹10–20 per maund as mill demand softened and arrivals rose.

title: US WROs double to 8: Will global apparel sourcing face more scrutiny?
summary:
Firemount’s US garment WRO, issued by CBP in November 2025, remains in force after its first anniversary and covers all garments, apparel and textiles made by the Mauritius company.
CBP extended similar orders in June 2026 to Jordan’s Needle Craft Ltd and Casual Wear Apparel LLC, citing forced-labour indicators.
CBP issued eight WROs in FY2026, double FY2025, as scrutiny widened beyond Asia.

title: Türkiye renews yarn duties on 7 Asian origins for 5 Years. Who pays?
summary:
Turkiye has renewed antidumping duties on specified staple-fibre yarn from seven Asian origins for five years, with existing rates unchanged.
Covered yarn imports rose 2.8 per cent to $185.96 million in January–September; targeted suppliers accounted for 62.5 per cent.
India remains the top targeted supplier, China gained share, and knitted-fabric and apparel exports are under pressure.

title: UKITMC to connect Indian manufacturers with UK firms at India ITME
summary:
UKITMC, a BTMA initiative, supported by the UK Government, will connect Indian manufacturers with British textile technology companies at India ITME 2026, to be held from 4–9 December.
UKITMC will host a dedicated industry networking event at the exhibition.
British technology providers will offer solutions for reducing costs, improving quality and minimising waste.

title: India’s polyester raw material prices fall as PTA, PSF weaken
summary:
India’s polyester raw material market stayed bearish in the week to November 21, 2026, as RIL cut PTA, polyester melt and PSF prices amid weak downstream demand.
PTA fell ₹4.70 (~$0.05) per kg to ₹93.90, melt declined ₹4.05 to ₹104.89 and PSF was cut by ₹4 per kg, while MEG stayed at ₹71.
CFR China PTA and MEG saw sharp volatility but ended lower over five sessions.

title: India & Canada conclude sixth CEPA talks in New Delhi
summary:
India and Canada have concluded the sixth negotiating round for the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement in New Delhi, with both sides stressing a balanced pact and market access. 
Talks from November 11-20, 2026, covered goods, services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion. 
The pact would support trade, investment and resilient supply chains.

title: ITMA ASIA to return to Singapore in 2029 under CEMATEX strategy
summary:
CEMATEX will bring ITMA ASIA back to Singapore from 23–26 October 2029, targeting growth markets across Asia and beyond.
A longer exhibition cycle aims to give textile technologies time to mature and deliver greater value for exhibitors and visitors.
CEMATEX and Japan’s JTMA will also explore emerging regions to help industry stakeholders access new markets and unlock further growth opportunities.

title: Labour groups put living wage for Bangladesh garment workers at $265
summary:
Nine international labour rights organisations have urged Bangladesh’s RMG Minimum Wage Board to set wages in line with living costs during the ongoing review. 
They cited a living-wage estimate of about Tk 33,000 (~$265), alongside worker proposals of Tk 32,000 for skilled workers and Tk 30,000 for trainees. 
The groups also asked buyers to absorb increases and avoid shifting orders.

title: South Korea's Misto Holdings mentors future textile, fashion talent
summary:
South Korea's Misto Holdings participated in the 2026 Mentoring Academic Camp, offering textile and fashion students industry exposure.
Around 20 participants visited its headquarters for business presentations, workplace tours and career mentoring.
Students also toured KOTITI Testing & Research Institute to gain insights into textile quality, testing and research, supporting industry talent.

title: 341 factories shut amid Bangladesh’s $13.75 bn garment rebound
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel rebound faces 341 factory closures ahead of wage talks, with disruption losses estimated at Tk30–40 billion (~$241–322 million).
July–October exports rose 5.82 per cent to $13.75 billion, but EU and US import data signal weaker demand.
TexPro flags buyer-market concentration and reliance on Chinese and Indian inputs.

title: Bangladesh's garment sector loses $682 mn amid labour unrest: BGMEA
summary:
Bangladesh's garment sector has suffered losses of around $682 million across 317 factories due to labour unrest, production disruptions and relocated export orders, according to BGMEA. 
The losses include $428 million in disrupted production and $254 million in orders shifted to other countries over November 1-18, the association said.

title: US-China truce: Garment exports up 19.7%; will port fees raise costs?
summary:
US-China trade truce expires on January 10, 2027 with no tariff changes announced, leaving main US duties on Chinese garments outside the truce.
Chinese cotton knit T-shirts carry a combined 36.5 per cent US duty, against 29 per cent for Vietnam and 26.5 per cent for Bangladesh and India.
US port-fee suspensions and 178 Section 301 exclusions end on January 9 unless extended.

title: Bahrain's apparel imports plunge 21.8% in Jan-Sept 2026
summary:

All top five suppliers recorded lower values; China led with 38.19 per cent share as shipments dropped 21.7 per cent to $67.76 million.
India, Bangladesh, Turkiye and Italy also declined, though Bangladesh lifted its share to 10.90 per cent.

title: Bangladesh leads EU denim market as exports fall 5.48% in Jan-Sep
summary:
Bangladesh remained the EU’s largest denim supplier in January–September 2026, accounting for 29.48 per cent of imports. 
EU purchases from Bangladesh fell 5.48 per cent year on year to €1.01 billion, outpacing the 3.24 per cent decline in overall denim imports. 
In September alone, shipments from Bangladesh rose 0.70 per cent YoY to €143 million.

title: New Zealand's apparel imports rise 12% YoY in October 2026
summary:

However, modest January-October growth and weaker cumulative non-knitted apparel exports showed that the clothing trade recovery remained uneven overall.

title: Can South Africa’s apparel manufacturers stay competitive?
summary:
Levi Strauss has proposed closing its Epping facility in Cape Town, putting more than 400 jobs at risk, as per reports.
The company has begun Section 189 consultations under South Africa’s Labour Relations Act and says no final decision will be made before talks end.
AGOA uncertainty, rising costs and underused capacity are cited as pressures on local clothing and textile competitiveness.

title: Bangladesh's RMG unrest causes daily losses of up to $176 mn: BGBA
summary:
Bangladesh is losing Tk 2,000-2,200 crore (~$160-176 million) in daily output due to RMG production disruption, BGBA has said.
It put cumulative losses from factory closures and road blockades at Tk 3,000-4,000 crore (~$240-320 million).
The association warned export shipments, buyer confidence, future orders and factory operations could be hit unless the wage dispute is resolved.
